name: devcontainercheck
one_liner: Static linter for devcontainer.json files - flags twelve shape defects enabling supply-chain, lifecycle-command, and host-escape attacks against VS Code / GitHub Codespaces / Dev Containers CLI consumers.
problem: The Microsoft dev containers specification defines six lifecycle slots - initializeCommand, onCreateCommand, updateContentCommand, postCreateCommand, postStartCommand, postAttachCommand - that execute on container create / attach. Opening a folder in VS Code with a devcontainer.json runs those commands once the folder is marked trusted; GitHub Codespaces and the Dev Containers CLI run them unconditionally. The October 2026 GhostAction supply-chain campaign (The Hacker News 2026-10-09, GitGuardian 2026-10-09, Socket 2026-10) escalated this fault class across tens of thousands of repositories: tag-pinned install commands and credential-exposing CI configurations exfiltrated maintainer secrets at scale. devcontainercheck lints the shape of the artifact developers already have on disk - devcontainer.json or .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, both plain JSON and JSONC - and flags twelve defects on a 5 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 2 INFO split: DC-001 lifecycle command pipes curl / wget / Invoke-WebRequest into bash / sh / python (the fetch-and-exec supply-chain shape); DC-002 lifecycle command runs pip install git+ / git clone from a URL without an @<40-hex-SHA> pin; DC-003 features entry references an OCI image / Git URL / HTTP tarball without an @sha256:<digest> or @<40-hex-SHA> pin; DC-004 credential-shaped literal (JWT / AWS / GitHub / PEM / bearer) inlined under containerEnv / remoteEnv / build.args / runArgs; DC-005 hidden-character class (Plane 14 TAG, bidi overrides, zero-width, mid-string BOM, control, PUA) in any string value; DC-006 mounts bind-mounts a sensitive host path (Docker socket, home .ssh / .aws / .gnupg / .kube, filesystem root); DC-007 runArgs grants a container-escape-relevant capability (--privileged, --pid=host, --net=host, --cap-add=sys_admin, --security-opt=seccomp=unconfined); DC-008 lifecycle command writes to a shell init file (.bashrc, .zshrc, .profile); DC-009 containerEnv / remoteEnv exposes a sensitive host variable via ${localEnv:...} (TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, cloud credentials); DC-010 image references a mutable tag (:latest / :main / :nightly) rather than @sha256:<digest>; DC-011 missing remoteUser / containerUser (container runs as root); DC-012 missing name field at the document level. Independent implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft, the containers.dev working group, or any of the cited security publications.
clean_room: Rules are derived from the public containers.dev specification (https://containers.dev/implementors/json_reference/) and from the public VS Code Workspace Trust documentation; from the public news coverage of the October 2026 GhostAction GitHub Actions supply-chain campaign (thehackernews.com/2026/10 credential-stealing-github-actions, blog.gitguardian.com ghostaction-github-actions-supply-chain-attack-returns, securitylabs.datadoghq.com); and from long-published public shape conventions for OCI image references (@sha256:<64hex>), VCS install pinning (@<40-hex-SHA>), and dotfile-shell-init paths. No Microsoft- or community-published linter reference implementation was read, vendored, or mirrored. Rule semantics are shape-only: a devcontainer.json is a developer-authored artifact that lives on disk and is read by consumers; shape defects at that layer are detectable statically.
